parameters.sampling: stratified across each vendor's collections, seeded

data_use_note: TCIA data are subject to the TCIA Data Usage Policy and each collection's own licence. The per-series licence recorded in these results must be reproduced in any publication, together with the collection name and the access date.

tag_absence.reconstructability_note: 'fallback_feasibility_rate' is marginal (over all screened series, including those that already carry a recorded CTDIvol). 'conditional_reconstructability_rate' is over the series that lack one, which is the population the reconstruction exists to serve. Report both: the marginal rate describes the archive, the conditional rate describes the method.

diagnostic_and_collimation_measured.note: Diagnostic acquisitions (recorded CTDIvol >= 0.5 mGy) whose header records total collimation. This is the stratum that isolates the dose model from the archive's metadata gaps, and the one to quote as the method's accuracy. Check 'vendor_by_collimation_provenance' first: collimation availability is itself vendor-dependent, so this stratum is not balanced across vendors.

diagnostic_acquisitions_only.note: Restricted to series whose recorded CTDIvol is at least 0.5 mGy. Below that the recorded value belongs to a localiser or another non-diagnostic acquisition, and comparing it against a reconstruction of the diagnostic series compares two different irradiations. Those cases are kept in 'overall' and in the per-case rows; this stratum is the one to quote.

by_collimation_provenance.note: The over-beaming factor grows roughly as 1/collimation once the collimation falls below the scanner's reference beam width, so a series whose header omits total collimation -- leaving it to be rebuilt from table feed, or in the worst case from slice thickness -- has a much wider error than one that records it. The two strata are reported separately because pooling them would misattribute a missing-metadata problem to the dose model.

independence.note: Public archives contain re-releases of the same acquisition under different collection names (curated/synthetic variants, phantom repeats). Identical (recorded, estimated) pairs indicate such duplicates, so the cases are not fully independent and the effective sample size is the distinct count, not n.

fallback_error.note: percent_error is 100*(estimated - recorded)/recorded for CTDIvol. A positive value means the physics reconstruction overestimates the scanner's own recorded figure. Errors are reported as a distribution, not a single correction factor. Where the DICOM model name does not identify the scanner variant (bowtie / scan field of view, or acquisition mode), the median across candidate coefficient rows is used; 'best_case_if_model_variant_known' is the same set of cases scored with the closest candidate, i.e. an optimistic bound on what the method could do if the variant were recorded.
